about: Outside records about a seller: company registers, chambers of commerce, trade fairs, sanctions lists and website traffic. Used to look a seller up outside the page it sells on, in marketplace scans and website checks.
how_to_change: Each country has its own file next to this one (china.json, usa.json...). Safely reads the seller's country from the page and runs global.json plus that country's file. A country with no file gets global.json only.
sources: the outside records Safely will read. status 'planned' means not built yet; 'live' means Safely reads it now.
access: 'offline' (checked inside Safely, no internet), 'api' (free official API), 'download' (a public list file), 'scrape' (read the website), 'paid_api'.
cost: 'free', 'small_fee' or 'paid'. key_env: the name of the key in .env on the server (the key itself is never written here).
step: the build step that adds the source (see claude/databases-plan.md in the Safely project).
cards: same as b2b.json (warning_points, points_when_value, enabled). Every database card has group 'outside_records', so the extension and dashboard can show them in their own section.
Found = a good sign. Not found = NOT a warning. Only a false claim (fake company number, fake fair) or a sanctions match is a warning.

sources.name: Sanctions lists (US OFAC, UN)
sources.what_it_does: Is the company on a US or UN banned list? Downloaded once a day; only companies, whole names.

sources.name: EU sanctions list
sources.what_it_does: Is the company on the EU banned list? Downloaded once a day with the US and UN lists (same switch, SANCTIONS_CHECK_ENABLED); only companies, whole names.

sources.name: GLEIF (LEI register)
sources.what_it_does: Official world register of company IDs (LEI). Bigger companies only. Searched by the whole company name; needs GLEIF_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: Wayback Machine
sources.what_it_does: Since when the website has been saved by the Wayback Machine. Card "Website history"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: Tranco list
sources.what_it_does: Is the website among the 1 million most visited websites? Card "Website traffic"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: crt.sh
sources.what_it_does: When the website got its first security certificate. Card "Security certificate"; needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true.

sources.name: OpenCorporates
sources.what_it_does: Company registers of many countries in one place.

sources.name: Shipping records (Panjiva, ImportGenius)
sources.what_it_does: Does the company really ship goods?

cards.what_it_checks: Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is on the US (OFAC), UN or EU sanctions lists. A match is a warning (it may be another company with the same name); no match is a good sign but says nothing more. Needs SANCTIONS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is in the official GLEIF register (LEI). Registered in the seller's country is a good sign; listed as closed is a warning; the same name in another country, or not in the register, is information only and never adds to the score. Needs GLEIF_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the company number the supplier gives (China's 18-character code, Brazil's CNPJ, France's SIREN / SIRET / VAT number) is a real number: its check digits must add up. Checked inside Safely, no internet. A number that fails is a warning (made up or mistyped).

What the country's own register says about the company number (Brazil: Receita Federal via BrasilAPI; France: recherche-entreprises.api.gouv.fr, and INSEE's Sirene API when that does not answer and INSEE_API_KEY is set). Active under the same name is a good sign; another company's name is a warning; closed is a warning; not found is information only. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the EU VAT number the supplier gives (any EU country, written with its country code: FR..., DE..., IT...) is active in the EU's VIES register (free, no key). Active under the seller's name is a good sign; active under another company's name is a warning; not active is a smaller warning (VIES only lists numbers that may trade with other EU countries). Some countries never give the name. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is listed on the US stock market (SEC EDGAR's list of listed companies, downloaded once a day; free, no key). 'Listed company' is a good sign; 'Not on the stock market' is information only and is shown only for US sellers. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SEC_CONTACT_EMAIL in .env (the SEC asks for a contact email).

For US sellers only: whether a company with exactly the seller's name (legal or trade name) is registered with the US government in SAM.gov. Active is a good sign; excluded by the US government (barred from government work) is a warning; expired or not registered is information only. A basic key allows 10 lookups a day, so each answer is kept for 7 days and at most SAM_GOV_DAILY_LIMIT (10 when not set) lookups are made a day. Needs REGISTERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SAM_GOV_API_KEY in .env (the key expires after about 90 days).

Whether a company with exactly the seller's name is a member of a chamber of commerce whose member pages are public: the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce (HKGCC, for Hong Kong and China sellers) or the thousands of local chambers on ChamberMaster / GrowthZone (for US sellers and sellers with no country file). One Google search (Serper) finds the member page, which is then opened to read the name. A member is a good sign; a member whose website differs from the seller's is information only (maybe another company with the same name); not a member shows no card. Needs CHAMBERS_CHECK_ENABLED=true and SERPER_API_KEY in .env.

Since when the Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) has saved the seller's own website. Saved over a year ago is a good sign; newer or never saved is information only and never adds to the score (a brand-new domain is already warned about by 'Website age'). Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

Whether the seller's own website is among the world's 1 million most visited websites (Tranco list). In the list is a good sign; not in it is information only (normal for small companies). Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.

When the seller's own website got its first security certificate (crt.sh, the public log of certificates). Over a year ago is a good sign; recent or none found is information only. Needs WEBSITE_RECORDS_CHECK_ENABLED=true in .env.
